correctness.rationale: The coprime Euclid-parametrization gives exactly four primitive smooth-leg possibilities; each is checked algebraically. Every edge is their smooth multiple. Exponent residues 0 or 1 modulo 5 give the explicit lower bound; the five-cycle, padding by coordinate maximum edge shifts and torus averaging give the upper bound. The bounds squeeze the density to 2/5. Exact standard-library checks matched all edges for 120 rectangular boxes, confirmed five hypotenuses and construction independence. Exact finite maxima are not claimed.

originality.rationale: The 2026 prime-power box upper and lower theorems concern a number of supported primes that increases with the box parameter and do not imply any positive fixed-three-prime density. General multiplicative-density regularity also does not imply this specific semigroup relative density. Known fixed-two-prime graph paths cannot yield the three-prime 5-cycle obstruction. Actual mathematical-result searches found no dominating statement; possible unindexed results are a documented risk.
residual_risks: An earlier unindexed or implicit fixed-support lattice graph independence theorem could contain the same two-fifths constant.

The classification of the four small supported primitive pairs may independently be classical; originality is asserted for the matching asymptotic extremal theorem, not for the existence of these four triples.

value.rationale: The invariant is the natural maximum of a no-Pythagorean-pair subset in exponent boxes over exactly the first three primes, motivated by the published general prime-power box program. The result determines its previously unknown large-box constant exactly (2/5), with a structural primitive-ratio graph, explicit 5-cycle upper certificate, and matching modular lower construction. The threshold from two support primes to three is mathematically meaningful; this is not an arbitrary finite cutoff or a restatement of known triple lists.
